title: The Drained Basin
subtitle: A 1970s swimming pool reclaimed by light.
line: Walk into a 1970s interior where water has retreated to leave only the architecture of light behind.
quote: To inhabit the void is to see through the glass of memory.
synopsis: You step into a cavernous, empty pool, where the polished concrete floors echo with the ghost of water. Guided by the liminal concrete strip, you approach the repurposed diving platform, a monumental anchor in the center of the drained basin. As you wander, four suspended light refractors cast dancing beams across the eyewear displays, simulating the shimmer of a submerged world. The experience concludes at a minimal concrete counter, grounding your descent into this architectural reverie.

why.d: A floor strip (liminal transition zone) runs 4.7 m from the door toward the hero (repurposed diving platform). The concrete strip forces a deliberate, reverent descent into the depth of the space.

why.d: The hero stands alone 5.6 m inside the door, 3.5 m tall; nothing else rises above 1.8 m. The towering diving platform focuses your attention, making the surrounding void feel vast and silent.

why.t: The glass refractors break the daylight
why.d: Four product stations (suspended light refractors) ring it loosely, 0.4 m from the route at the closest. The glass refractors break the daylight, transforming the air into a shimmering, fluid-like atmosphere.

why.d: The pay counter (minimal concrete counter) sits at the back right, where the route ends. The concrete counter provides a final, grounded anchor before you exit the hollowed expanse.
